title: Rollout checklist — Tiered SLOs + Error Budgets (Hosted vs Dedicated)
content:
Doc owner: Aisha Bello (SRE)
Last reviewed: 2026-02-14
Audience: SRE, Platform (Routing/Control Plane), Infra/Fleet, Telemetry, Product (Hosted/Dedicated)

Purpose
This checklist is the go/no-go and sequencing guide for rolling out tiered SLIs/SLOs and error budget enforcement across Hosted (shared) and Dedicated (reserved capacity). It’s written for an incremental rollout: staging → production (shadow) → warn-only → enforced.

Definitions (quick)
- Tiers in scope: Hosted, Dedicated
- Primary SLIs:
  - Success rate: non-5xx for valid requests (per SLI spec exclusions)
  - Latency: end-to-end gateway→response (p50/p95/p99, per endpoint class)
  - Streaming reliability: stream disconnect/error events counted per spec (exclude client abort where detectable)
- Reporting windows (program default unless overridden per tier): 28d rolling for budget; multi-window burn-rate alerts per ADR-0143

Rollout principle
- Measurement correctness > enforcement. We do not enable deploy gating until we can demonstrate tier tagging correctness and SLI coverage.
- Enforcement phases:
  1) Dashboards only (no paging)
  2) Paging burn-rate alerts + incident triggers
  3) Deploy gate warn-only
  4) Deploy gate enforced for non-emergency deploys

====================================================================
PHASE 0 — Preflight (owners: SRE + Telemetry + Routing)
Target: before staging validation begins

[ ] Confirm canonical SLI spec is published and reviewed
    - Link: Confluence SLI specification (API gateway + routing)
    - Acceptance: spec includes exclusions for invalid requests, rate-limited (429), explicit client abort handling, and retry/fallback accounting.
    - Owner: Allison Grant

[ ] Confirm tier tagging decision + implementation plan
    - Link: ADR-0142 and tier-tagging-metrics-plan
    - Acceptance: tags are set at ingress and propagated through routing/fallback, tracing, and metrics; documented tag keys + allowed values.
    - Owner: Amara Diallo / Ravi Menon

[ ] Confirm SLO config schema and required fields
    - Link: PR-28438 + ENG-4926
    - Acceptance: schema supports tier + region + endpoint class; includes SLI query references; supports safe rollout flags (shadow/disabled/enforced).
    - Owner: Logan Wright / Jordan Lee

[ ] Confirm initial SLO targets approved by PM
    - Link: tiered-slo-targets-working-sheet + PM-812
    - Acceptance: Hosted vs Dedicated targets exist for each in-scope endpoint class and region; explicitly notes any “N/A” and rationale.
    - Owner: Nikhil Sharma / Lauren Bishop

[ ] Confirm region list and label normalization
    - Acceptance: single canonical region naming across gateway metrics, routing logs, and dashboard filters (avoid us-east-1 vs use1 drift).
    - Owner: Miles Thornton / Thomas Baird

====================================================================
PHASE 1 — Staging validation (owners: SRE + Routing + Telemetry)
Target: staging burn-in 3–5 business days

1. Tier tagging + propagation tests
[ ] Tag presence at ingest
    - Verify metrics include tier tag for 99.9%+ of requests in staging.
    - Acceptance: missing tier tag < 0.1% and attributable to known test traffic.
    - Owner: Amara Diallo

[ ] Tag integrity through routing/fallback
    - Create forced fallback scenario (capacity constrained or policy-based) and verify tier tag remains original tier.
    - Acceptance: SLI event taxonomy marks fallback but does not reclassify tier.
    - Owner: Mina Haddad / Elena Popov

[ ] Cardinality guardrails
    - Verify we do NOT emit per-request-id labels; per-customer is only emitted where explicitly allowed (Dedicated dashboards with access controls).
    - Acceptance: top label cardinality stable; no unexpected new high-cardinality dimensions.
    - Owner: Thomas Baird

2. SLI calculation correctness (spot checks)
[ ] Success rate semantics
    - Inject controlled errors: 400/401/429 and 5xx; confirm only qualifying requests count against success SLI.
    - Acceptance: 4xx (invalid/auth) excluded; 429 excluded; 5xx included.
    - Owner: Rafael Mendes

[ ] Latency measurement points
    - Confirm “start” and “end” timestamps match the spec for chat/completions vs embeddings vs streaming.
    - Acceptance: streaming latency uses time-to-first-token and/or stream completion as defined; documented in dashboard.
    - Owner: Sergio Costa / Felix Schneider

[ ] Streaming disconnect classification
    - Simulate: client abort, upstream disconnect, gateway timeout, model server crash mid-stream.
    - Acceptance: client abort excluded (where detectable); infra/service disconnect included; taxonomy is visible in logs and metrics.
    - Owner: Peter Holtz

3. Dashboard/alert preview in staging
[ ] Tiered SLO dashboards load and filter correctly
    - Link: observability-pack/pr-6312
    - Acceptance: dashboard has tier switcher, endpoint class filters, region breakdown, and “top contributors” (route/model) without blowing cardinality.
    - Owner: Sergio Costa

[ ] Recording rules produce expected time series
    - Link: redwood/pr-28492
    - Acceptance: burn-rate numerator/denominator series non-empty; no NaN spikes from missing data.
    - Owner: Caleb Johnson

[ ] Alert routing smoke test (no paging)
    - Fire test alert to verify it lands in correct Slack channel + on-call tool (suppressed from paging in staging).
    - Owner: Sean Gallagher (delegate: Rafael Mendes)

====================================================================
PHASE 2 — Backfill + data quality checks (owners: Telemetry + SRE)
Target: before production dashboards are considered reliable

[ ] Metric coverage validation
    - Run SLO toolkit validator for every {tier, endpoint class, region} in scope.
    - Acceptance: 100% coverage or documented exception with mitigation plan.
    - Link: slo-toolkit/pr-418
    - Owner: Logan Wright

[ ] Backfill budget computation (if applicable)
    - If we backfill last N days for trendline: confirm backfill job completion + correctness.
    - Acceptance: backfill aligns within ±0.1% absolute to spot-checked raw query results.
    - Owner: Caleb Johnson / Aisha Bello

[ ] Missing-data policy confirmed
    - Decide and document: do we treat missing metrics as “bad” or “unknown” for budget? (Default: unknown with explicit ‘data quality’ alert.)
    - Acceptance: data-quality alert exists and is separate from burn-rate.
    - Owner: Allison Grant

[ ] Data lag / freshness SLI for observability pipeline
    - Acceptance: dashboard shows ingestion lag; alerts if lag > threshold (e.g., 10m) to avoid false burn/non-burn.
    - Owner: Logan Wright

====================================================================
PHASE 3 — Production: dashboards live, alerts in shadow (no paging)
Target: 1 week (minimum) to observe baseline + tune

[ ] Roll out dashboards to production (read-only)
    - Dedicated dashboards restricted via RBAC.
    - Acceptance: CS/SE access process defined (INT helpdesk) but not broadly granted by default.
    - Owner: Chloe Martin / Rachel Kim

[ ] “Shadow” burn-rate alert evaluation
    - Alerts run but do not page; results posted to eng-sre channel daily for review.
    - Acceptance: false positives < 2/day; obvious misses investigated.
    - Owner: Sergio Costa / Aisha Bello

[ ] Establish baseline budget burn expectations
    - Capture: typical Hosted burn-rate during peak, and Dedicated steady-state by region.
    - Acceptance: documented baseline with at least 5 weekdays of data.
    - Owner: Miles Thornton

[ ] Validate tier labeling for real customer traffic
    - Sample: Dedicated accounts (2–3) + Hosted (global) and check tier tag consistency from gateway logs → routing traces → metrics.
    - Acceptance: no evidence of Dedicated traffic being labeled Hosted (or vice versa).
    - Owner: Rafael Mendes

====================================================================
PHASE 4 — Production: paging burn-rate alerts + incident process enabled
Target: 1–2 weeks before deploy gating

[ ] Enable paging for burn-rate alerts
    - Link: ENG-4930 + PR-28492
    - Acceptance: multi-window burn-rate thresholds per ADR-0143; routes to correct on-call rotation; severity mapping documented.
    - Owner: Rafael Mendes

[ ] Incident trigger criteria agreed
    - Link: error-budget-breach-incident-process
    - Acceptance: burn-rate at “fast burn” threshold triggers incident creation within X minutes and named IC/Comms/Scribe.
    - Owner: Sean Gallagher

[ ] Runbook is current and linked from alerts
    - Link: error-budget-breach-mitigation-runbook
    - Acceptance: alert annotations include runbook URL + dashboard deep link + recent deploy list.
    - Owner: Peter Holtz

[ ] Infra escalation path validated (Dedicated prioritization)
    - Link: capacity-mitigation-guidelines-for-slo-events + dedicated-vs-hosted-capacity-prioritization-notes
    - Acceptance: clear criteria for adding capacity vs shifting traffic; Dedicated headroom targets documented.
    - Owner: Neha Kapoor (delegate: Infra on-call lead)

[ ] Customer comms pathway verified (Dedicated)
    - Link: tiered-status-communications-guidelines
    - Acceptance: comms templates exist for tier-specific impact; Dedicated comms owners are on the page.
    - Owner: Jasmine Liu / Rachel Kim

====================================================================
PHASE 5 — Deploy gate: warn-only
Target: 1–2 weeks

[ ] Deploy gate wired to current budget state
    - Link: ENG-4935 + PR-28510
    - Acceptance: for a tier in fast burn / red budget state, deployments emit warning in CI/CD + Slack; override requires reason and is logged.
    - Owner: Jordan Lee / Connor O'Brien

[ ] Emergency fix pathway documented
    - Acceptance: “break glass” label/process exists, includes post-deploy review requirement.
    - Owner: Sahana Iyer

[ ] Validate gate behavior with simulated red budget
    - Acceptance: warning triggers for non-critical service deploy; does not block.
    - Owner: Benji Okafor

====================================================================
PHASE 6 — Deploy gate: enforced for non-emergency deploys
Target: after stability in warn-only (>= 2 weeks recommended)

[ ] Enforce release freeze when budget exhausted (non-emergency)
    - Link: ENG-4941 + PR-28541
    - Acceptance: non-emergency deploys blocked when tier is in “budget exhausted” state; emergency overrides are permitted and logged.
    - Owner: Connor O'Brien

[ ] Exception process and approval ladder
    - Acceptance: documented approvers (SRE Director or VP Infra/Reliability depending on scope), and required evidence (mitigation plan + rollback strategy).
    - Owner: Sean Gallagher / Neha Kapoor

====================================================================
Training + enablement checklist (parallel work; must be complete by Phase 4)

[ ] On-call training session (SRE + Routing + Infra)
    - Content: how to interpret tiered dashboards, burn-rate alerts, streaming failure taxonomy, mitigation levers (traffic shaping, fallback, capacity).
    - Acceptance: recorded session + link shared; attendance from primary rotations.
    - Owner: Aisha Bello

[ ] CS/SE enablement: “how to answer SLO questions”
    - Content: definitions, exclusions, where to view Dedicated SLO dashboards, what to collect in escalations.
    - Link: slo-escalation-intake-template
    - Acceptance: CS playbook updated and validated with at least 1 real ticket walk-through.
    - Owner: Markus Klein / Rachel Kim

[ ] Access control process for Dedicated dashboards
    - Acceptance: RBAC groups created; request process documented; audit trail retained.
    - Owner: Chloe Martin

====================================================================
Go / No-Go criteria (hard gates)
All must be TRUE to proceed from Phase 3 → Phase 4 (paging), and Phase 5 → Phase 6 (enforcement).

To enable paging (Phase 4):
- [ ] Tier tags present and correct on >= 99.9% of production requests (per tier) OR missingness is fully explained and limited to known test traffic.
- [ ] SLI queries produce non-empty series in all in-scope regions for 7 consecutive days.
- [ ] Data freshness/lag monitored and within threshold 95%+ of the time.
- [ ] False positive review completed: no more than 2 “no-actionable” pages per week in shadow mode.
- [ ] Runbook linked and confirmed usable by on-call (dry-run completed).

To enable enforced deploy gating (Phase 6):
- [ ] At least 2 weeks of warn-only gate with override logs reviewed.
- [ ] Emergency override process tested and documented.
- [ ] Product (Hosted + Dedicated) sign-off that enforcement aligns with SLA/SLO mapping expectations.

Sign-offs (record date + approver in change log)
- SRE: Sean Gallagher
- Telemetry: Logan Wright
- Routing: Mina Haddad
- Infra: Neha Kapoor (or delegate)
- Product Hosted: Nikhil Sharma
- Product Dedicated: Lauren Bishop

====================================================================
Rollback / disable plan (if rollout causes harm)

Triggers for rollback/disable:
- Severe metric cardinality increase impacting ingestion or query reliability
- Widespread missing tier tags with unknown root cause
- Paging storm due to bad query / recording rule bug

Actions:
1) Flip SLO config to disable enforcement (keep dashboards) for affected tier/region/endpoint.
2) Disable burn-rate paging (keep shadow evaluation) if alert bug.
3) Revert recent recording rule change and backfill impacted series.
4) Postmortem required for any enforcement-related production disruption.

Operational notes / TODOs
- TODO: confirm final list of “endpoint classes” for SLO grouping (chat/completions vs embeddings vs rerank vs streaming) matches routing taxonomy.
- TODO: confirm how we treat “graceful degradation” (fallback model variant) in success SLI and latency SLI for Dedicated.
- TODO: decide whether to show customer-facing budget status (Dedicated) in Console v1 or keep internal-only until Q2.
